title: The End Of Upward Mobility | NOEMA
gist: Branko Milanović and Nils Gilman argue that the 'homoploutic' class — people in the top decile of both labor and capital income (~3% of Americans) — has underpinned 40 years of meritocratic legitimacy, and that AI will either entrench it into a hereditary aristocracy or dissolve its wage premium into pure rentierism. Either way meritocratic legitimacy collapses, producing a feudal-shaped class pyramid that could make rich AI societies more politically unstable than poorer ones.

insights.claim: James Burnham's 1941 'The Managerial Revolution' wrongly predicted managers would displace capitalists; instead managers rose into capital and became capitalists themselves.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Frames who owns AI as the key to predicting the next ruling class.

insights.so_what: Applied to AI: ownership of models is the locus of future economic and political power.

insights.claim: Roughly 30% of the top U.S. income decile — about 3% of the total population — are homoplouts, in the top decile for labor, capital and total income; the share has risen steadily since the early 1980s, tracking rising inequality and falling mobility.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: The US elite's dual-income structure is unusually entrenched vs peers; relevant for wealth-management and luxury demand durability.
insights.quote: roughly 30% of the top American income decile qualifies — that is, 3% of the total U.S. population
insights.locator: It isn’t just the fact

insights.claim: The homoploutic class is below 1% of the population in Mexico (similar in Brazil, Peru, Colombia) and around 2-2.5% in Spain, Italy, Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden, making the United States the most extreme case.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Cross-country class structure differences imply differing AI-disruption exposure by country.
insights.locator: Compare this to Mexico

insights.claim: 60% of American households have zero or negligible cash income from capital, vs 79% in Spain, 93% in Colombia and 96% in Peru as of 2021.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Most households lack exposure to capital income, so AI-driven capital-share gains will be narrowly distributed.
insights.quote: Sixty percent of American households have zero or negligible cash income from capital ownership.
insights.locator: As bad as inequality of income

insights.claim: The Gini coefficient of U.S. capital income is about twice that of disposable income; the top 1% of American capitalists received nearly $100,000 per person in capital income in 2022.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Extreme capital-income concentration shapes political pressure for capital taxation as AI raises capital's share.
insights.locator: As bad as inequality of income

insights.claim: Homoplouts proper earn about $20,548 per person (north of $80,000 per family) from capital income — a solid floor beneath a high salary.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Quantifies the capital cushion of the professional elite that AI wage compression would expose.
insights.locator: As bad as inequality of income

insights.claim: A household drawing both wages and capital income is hedged against both labor-market and stock-market shocks, internalizing and effectively eliminating class struggle — the one development that would have surprised Marx.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Explains elite political support for both property rights and credentialism; AI breaking the wage leg breaks the hedge.
insights.quote: The homoploutic household is exposed to both and therefore, in practice, to neither.
insights.locator: A pure wage-earner is exposed

insights.claim: Per Daniel Markovits, parental investment separating an elite child from a middle-class child by the end of graduate school is equivalent to a roughly $10 million inheritance per child.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Elite education spending is a quasi-inheritance channel; AI eroding its payoff threatens the education-premium industry.

insights.claim: Marx's M–C–M' circuit becomes M–E–M' for the homoploutic class, where E is children's education; if E is out of reach for non-homoplouts, class mobility has effectively closed.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Education is the reproduction mechanism of elite wealth; watch its returns under AI.

insights.claim: The homoploutic class's legitimacy rested on the message 'we are rich because we are useful' with a narrow but real path for others to join.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: If this legitimation fails, expect stronger redistribution politics.

insights.claim: Key uncertainties: whether AI raises total labor output or merely shifts production from humans to machines, whether capabilities keep advancing given circular data-center financing and political backlash, and how fast productive adoption happens.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Circular data-center financing and backlash are named risks to the AI capability trajectory.
insights.quote: We don’t know whether AI will raise our total labor output or merely shift production from human labor to machines without expanding the total.
insights.locator: Much is still unknown.

insights.claim: Which future prevails hinges on one unresolved empirical question: whether AI substitutes for or complements high-premium cognitive labor.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN

insights.claim: In the entrenchment scenario, capital's share of national income rises with AI deployment while Schumpeterian destruction holds up the profit rate, so homoplouts thicken from a third to half or two-thirds of the top labor-income decile and become a self-reproducing hardworking aristocracy.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Supports long capital-owner/AI-equity exposure and the wealth-management franchise of the top decile.
insights.locator: The first possible future is elite

insights.claim: In the dissolution scenario, AI substitutes for the high-premium cognitive work (lawyers, financiers, consultants, software engineers, doctors) that LLMs perform most convincingly, collapsing the elite wage premium and reverting homoplouts to pure rentiers like Mexico's classical pattern.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Professional-services and education-premium business models are exposed if AI substitutes for knowledge work.
insights.locator: The second alternate future is class

insights.claim: Moravec's paradox implies high-level reasoning is easier to automate than sensorimotor skills, making elite cognitive jobs more exposed than manual trades.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Favors relative resilience of skilled-trade and in-person service labor vs white-collar work.
insights.locator: The second alternate future is class

insights.claim: Under either scenario, the homoploutic class's claim to be a legitimate meritocracy collapses — under entrenchment because entry is closed, under dissolution because there is no meritorious activity left.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Expect legitimacy crises that drive populist wealth/capital taxation.
insights.locator: Under either scenario, the ideological

insights.claim: The AI-era social structure: a few thousand model owners at the summit, a closed homoploutic remnant, a service class (gardeners, aides, tradesmen) employed but not middle class, and a redundant population whose skills are obsolete.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Concentrated model ownership implies extreme returns to AI platform owners and pressure for UBI.
insights.quote: At the summit we find the few thousand people who own the models.
insights.locator: Around this reduced elite

insights.claim: The 20th-century assumption that development produces a large, stabilizing middle class may prove exceptional; AI could make the richest societies more politically turbulent than poorer ones, inverting modernization theory.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Raise political-risk premia on advanced economies, not just emerging markets.
insights.locator: What is striking about this pyramid

insights.claim: A large lumpen population with free time is ready kindling for political operators, and like the late Roman Republic, instability requires only one plutocrat deciding to mobilize malcontents against rivals.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Intra-elite conflict (e.g., tech billionaires mobilizing populism) is the key instability channel to watch.
insights.locator: The Roman analogy is relevant

insights.claim: A closed-off hierarchy is intolerable to democracy, which helps explain Silicon Valley's markedly anti-democratic turn described in Gil Duran's 'The Nerd Reich'.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Tech-elite political alignment is a regulatory and political-risk variable for AI firms.
insights.locator: A hierarchy that can be scaled

insights.claim: The roughly 40-year settlement in which the same people held the best jobs and the most property is ending; abundance advocates get the economics right but the politics wrong.
insights.speaker: BRANKO MILANOVIĆ AND NILS GILMAN
insights.so_what: Long-horizon regime change in distributional politics; position for higher redistribution risk.
insights.quote: Advocates of abundance who imagine machines doing the work while we enjoy our leisure have described the economics correctly and the politics not at all.
insights.locator: All we are reasonably sure of
